title: F30: triage termination is scope-blind — a fleet lane whose ONE scoped item is already done commits empty and seals FAIL
summary: Cycle 1682: the lane's fleet_scope pinned exactly one item (crossartifact-invariant-stack), which cycle 1679 had already shipped; triage correctly committed an empty top_n (dropped: already-shipped). decideTriageTermination then re-labelled the no-work end as triage-empty-commitment-claimable-work because hasClaimableInboxWork (go/internal/core/triage_termination.go) checks the WHOLE inbox, and with a nil predicate it also counts surface-routed items as claimable. The lane could claim none of that work, so the cycle sealed FAIL and reset the ship streak.
fix: Scope the claimable-work check to the lane: in fleet mode read the lane scope (cycleoutcome.LaneScopeIDs / lane-scope.json) and ask whether any SCOPED item is still claimable; inject the routing scope predicate (guards.IsProtectedScope) instead of nil so console-owned items never count. A lane whose scope holds no claimable item ends as triage-no-work (SKIPPED), not FAIL. Pin with the 1682 shape.
notes: Found in the 2026-09-26 census of cycles 1620-1688 (F29 research finding); the architecture review of F29 placed it in the same follow-up as re-selection. triage_termination.go is not on the protected manifest, but the orchestrator call sites are. | Architecture review 2026-09-26 (F35, MINOR 2): hasClaimableInboxWork partitions with a NIL predicate, so it disagrees with the claim floor on every surface-routed item — now also on an operator route:lane over a declared protected file (the claim refuses it; the termination check counts it claimable → triage-empty-commitment-claimable-work → FAIL). Inject the same routing-root predicate (or the F35c Surface port) here.
